bands.label: Thin
bands.blurb: Limited machine-readable signal beyond documentation a human can read.

providers.name: CMS Energy
providers.description: CMS Energy is an energy holding company whose primary subsidiary is Consumers Energy, an electric and natural gas utility serving customers in Michigan. Consumers Energy participates in the Green Button Connect My Data (GBCMD) program, exposing customer-authorized energy usage data to third parties via OAuth 2.0 - typically brokered through UtilityAPI - for use in energy management, demand response, EV charging, solar, and sustainability applications.

providers.name: Xcel Energy
providers.description: Xcel Energy is a major U.S. electricity and natural gas utility holding company headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota, providing service to approximately 3.7 million electricity customers and 2.1 million natural gas customers across eight Midwestern and Western states: Colorado, Minnesota, Texas, New Mexico, North Dakota, South Dakota, Michigan, and Wisconsin. Xcel Energy operates a developer portal at developer-apim.aws.xcelenergy.com that organizes APIs across customer account management, billing, payments, product and service offerings, and request service. The company provides Green Button Connect My Data APIs based on the ESPI (Energy Services Provider Interface) standard developed by NAESB, enabling authorized third-party applications to access customer energy usage data via OAuth 2.0. Xcel Energy also supports IEEE 2030.5 protocol on newer Itron Gen 5 Riva smart meters for direct local-network access to real-time energy data including solar production. Beyond data APIs, Xcel Energy is a Fortune 500 company investing in clean energy, grid modernization, electric vehicle programs, demand response, and renewable energy interconnection.

providers.name: Pg And E
providers.description: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E) is one of the largest combined natural gas and electric energy companies in the United States, serving approximately 16 million people in northern and central California. PG&E offers the Share My Data API, a Green Button Connect My Data implementation providing customer- authorized access to energy usage interval data for both electricity and gas through RESTful web services.

providers.name: Southern Company
providers.description: Southern Company is a leading American gas and electric utility holding company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. Through its subsidiaries — Alabama Power, Georgia Power, Mississippi Power, Southern Natural Gas, and Southern Company Gas — it serves 9 million gas and electric utility customers across 6 states. Southern Company is a Fortune 500 company with operations spanning electricity generation, transmission, distribution, and natural gas distribution.

providers.name: WEC Energy Group
providers.description: WEC Energy Group (NYSE: WEC) is one of the nation's premier energy companies, serving 4.4 million customers across Wisconsin, Illinois, Michigan, and Minnesota with electricity and natural gas service. The company operates through regional utilities including We Energies, Wisconsin Public Service, Peoples Gas, North Shore Gas, Minnesota Energy Resources, Michigan Gas Utilities, and Upper Michigan Energy Resources. WEC Energy Group offers customer-facing digital services including account management portals, mobile apps, and Green Button energy usage data access.

providers.name: Southwest Gas
providers.description: Southwest Gas Holdings is a natural gas distribution company that purchases, distributes, and transports natural gas for customers in Arizona, Nevada, and California. As a Fortune 1000 utility company headquartered in Las Vegas, Nevada, Southwest Gas serves over 2 million customers through its regulated utility segment and also operates Centuri Group, a full-service utility infrastructure services company.

bands.label: Emerging
bands.blurb: More than an index entry but still mostly links rather than artifacts.

providers.name: Williams Companies
providers.description: Williams Companies is a Fortune 500 energy infrastructure company that operates approximately 33,000 miles of natural gas pipeline infrastructure, moving roughly one-third of the nation's natural gas. The company's flagship Transco pipeline system spans 10,000 miles from south Texas to New York City and is the nation's largest-volume natural gas pipeline. Williams provides pipeline transportation, gathering, processing, and storage services across key natural gas supply basins and serves utilities, power generators, industrial customers, and local distribution companies across the United States.

providers.name: UGI Corporation
providers.description: UGI Corporation is a Fortune 500 international energy distribution and services company headquartered in King of Prussia, Pennsylvania. UGI distributes natural gas, liquid propane, and electricity primarily through four business segments: UGI Utilities (natural gas and electric distribution in Pennsylvania), AmeriGas Propane (largest US propane marketer), Midstream and Marketing, and UGI International (European energy distribution). No public developer API has been identified; the company primarily uses EDI and utility industry standards for B2B data exchange.

providers.name: AES Corporation
providers.description: The AES Corporation is a Fortune 500 global energy company that generates and distributes electrical power. AES operates a diverse portfolio of renewable, thermal, LNG, and battery storage facilities across multiple countries, serving utilities, industrial facilities, and end users. AES is the largest global supplier of clean energy to corporations in the Americas and operates 34.7 GW globally with $12.2 billion in annual revenue. The company serves 18.7 million household equivalents through utilities in Indiana, Ohio, and El Salvador. AES also co-founded Fluence Energy, a leading energy storage and software platform company.

providers.name: Atmos Energy
providers.description: Atmos Energy is one of the largest natural-gas-only distributors in the United States, delivering natural gas to residential, commercial, public-authority, and industrial customers across multiple states including Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Tennessee, Colorado, Kansas, and Virginia. The company provides online account management, a Builder Portal for developers and contractors, and digital service request capabilities for natural gas connections and meter installations.

providers.name: Consolidated Edison
providers.description: Consolidated Edison, Inc. (Con Edison) is a Fortune 500 holding company that, through its subsidiaries, provides electric, natural gas, and steam service to customers in New York City and Westchester County. Con Edison does not publish a general-purpose developer portal; programmatic data access is delivered through the Green Button Connect My Data (GBC) program, which lets authorized third parties retrieve customer energy usage data via the NAESB Energy Services Provider Interface (ESPI) standard once the customer grants consent through Con Edison's authorization portal.

providers.name: CenterPoint Energy
providers.description: CenterPoint Energy is a domestic energy delivery company that provides electric transmission and distribution, natural gas distribution, and energy services operations serving residential, commercial, and industrial customers across multiple U.S. states. Developer-facing interfaces include the Smart Meter Texas (SMT) Usage History Inquiry API, Green Button Connect My Data exports for authorized third-party access to customer interval usage, and the Centerpoint Connect service API at api-portal.centerpointconnect.io used by contractor and field-service integrations.

providers.name: Constellation Energy
providers.description: Constellation Energy Corporation is a Fortune 500 clean-energy producer and competitive retail electricity and natural gas supplier in the United States, generating power from a fleet of nuclear, hydro, wind, and solar facilities. Constellation does not publish a public developer portal; programmatic interactions are delivered to enterprise and large commercial customers through the Energy Manager platform (account-managed onboarding, no public API specifications) and consumer interactions are handled through the My Constellation account portal. EDI 867 (usage) and 810 (invoice) remain the most common machine-to-machine integration paths and are arranged on a contract-by-contract basis.

providers.name: Ameren
providers.description: Ameren Corporation is a regulated electric and natural gas utility serving customers in Missouri and Illinois. The company provides reliable energy delivery, smart grid infrastructure, and renewable energy programs. Ameren Illinois implements the Green Button Connect My Data program (Share My Usage) based on the ESPI standard, enabling authorized third parties to access customer energy usage data. Ameren also operates a Renewables Portal for community solar generation owners and participates in grid modernization initiatives.

providers.name: Portland General Electric
providers.description: Portland General Electric is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Portland General Electric API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Exelon
providers.description: Exelon Corporation is one of the largest energy delivery companies in the United States, serving more than 10 million customers through its regulated electric and gas utility subsidiaries: Atlantic City Electric, BGE, ComEd, Delmarva Power, PECO, and Pepco. Headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, Exelon operates across multiple U.S. states. No public consumer-facing developer APIs have been identified for Exelon; customer self-service is conducted through utility portals.

providers.name: FirstEnergy
providers.description: FirstEnergy is one of the largest investor-owned electric systems in the United States, with utilities serving customers in Ohio, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, West Virginia, Maryland, and New York. FirstEnergy does not publish a public developer portal or open API catalog. Customer energy data is shared with authorized Curtailment Service Providers and Conservation Service Providers under its Third-Party Data Access program in Pennsylvania, and bulk utility data is exchanged with state regulators and grid operators through Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) and other industry-standard interfaces.

providers.name: Eversource Energy
providers.description: Eversource Energy is the largest energy delivery company in New England, providing electric, natural gas, and water service to millions of customers in Connecticut, Massachusetts, and New Hampshire.

providers.name: American Electric Power
providers.description: American Electric Power (AEP) is one of the largest electric utilities in the United States, delivering electricity to more than 5.6 million customers across 11 states through its regulated utility subsidiaries including AEP Ohio, AEP Texas, Appalachian Power, Indiana Michigan Power, Kentucky Power, Public Service Company of Oklahoma, and Southwestern Electric Power Company. AEP operates the nation's largest electricity transmission network spanning over 40,000 miles and maintains approximately 31,000 megawatts of generating capacity.

providers.name: Hubbell
providers.description: Hubbell is a global manufacturer of high-quality electrical and electronic products for non-residential and residential construction, industrial, and utility applications. The company has provided trusted infrastructure solutions since 1888 across power and utilities, lighting and controls, wiring and electrical, and datacom product categories serving commercial, data center, industrial, healthcare, telecom, and water and gas markets.

providers.name: MDU Resources Group
providers.description: MDU Resources Group is a diversified natural resources company with operations in regulated energy delivery, construction materials, and construction services. No public developer APIs are currently documented.

providers.name: Public Service Enterprise Group
providers.description: Public Service Enterprise Group (PSEG) is a publicly traded diversified energy holding company headquartered in Newark, New Jersey. Through its subsidiaries including PSE&G and PSEG Power, the company provides regulated electric and natural gas distribution and operates electric power generation across the northeastern United States. PSEG is a Fortune 500 company. No public developer APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Dominion Energy
providers.description: Dominion Energy is one of the nation's largest producers and transporters of energy, providing electricity and natural gas to customers across multiple U.S. states including Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio, and Utah. No public developer APIs are currently published.

providers.name: Hawaiian Electric Industries
providers.description: Hawaiian Electric Industries (HEI) is a Hawaii-based holding company whose primary subsidiaries provide electric utility service to roughly 95% of Hawaii's residents through Hawaiian Electric, and clean-energy investments through Pacific Current. HEI does not publish public developer APIs at this time; this index tracks the company and its subsidiaries for API discovery purposes.

providers.name: NextEra Energy
providers.description: NextEra Energy, Inc. is a Fortune 500 American energy company and one of the largest electric utility holding companies in the United States. It is the world's largest generator of renewable energy from the wind and sun, and a world leader in battery storage. NextEra Energy operates principally through its two subsidiaries, Florida Power & Light (FPL) and NextEra Energy Resources. This repository captures the public-facing digital surface, corporate touchpoints, and any developer or data resources for NextEra Energy. No public REST APIs, developer portal, or machine-readable data feeds have been identified at this time.

providers.name: PPL
providers.description: PPL Corporation is a U.S. energy company that delivers electricity and natural gas to customers through its regulated utilities in Pennsylvania, Kentucky, and Rhode Island. PPL is a Fortune 500 company.

providers.name: Entergy
providers.description: Entergy Corporation is an integrated energy company headquartered in New Orleans, Louisiana, providing electricity to more than 3 million utility customers across Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Texas. The company operates power generation, transmission, and distribution infrastructure including nuclear, renewable, and hydroelectric resources. While Entergy does not publish a public developer API portal, it operates customer-facing digital tools (myEntergy account portal, outage map, energy efficiency toolkit) that interact with internal systems via private APIs.

providers.name: NRG Energy
providers.description: NRG Energy is a Fortune 500 American energy company. This repository captures the APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts for NRG Energy. No public APIs have been documented at this time.

providers.name: Puget Energy
providers.description: Puget Energy is the parent company of Puget Sound Energy (PSE), a regulated electric and natural gas utility serving customers across Washington state. Headquartered in Bellevue, Washington, the company provides electricity and natural gas service, energy efficiency programs, outage management, and customer billing services. No public developer APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: NiSource
providers.description: NiSource is one of the largest fully-regulated utility companies in the United States, serving approximately 3.5 million natural gas and electric customers across six states through its operating subsidiaries Columbia Gas and NIPSCO.

providers.name: Talen Energy
providers.description: Talen Energy is an independent power producer and energy infrastructure company and a Fortune 1000 firm. The company operates a portfolio of nuclear, natural gas, oil, and renewable power generation facilities across the United States and supplies wholesale electricity into competitive markets. Talen Energy does not publish a public developer portal or external API.

providers.name: Dte Energy
providers.description: DTE Energy is a Detroit-based diversified energy company involved in the development and management of energy-related businesses and services nationwide, with utility operations in Michigan.

providers.name: Edison International
providers.description: Edison International is the parent company of Southern California Edison, one of the nation's largest electric utilities, and Edison Energy, a portfolio of competitive energy services.

providers.name: OGE Energy
providers.description: OGE Energy is the parent company of Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company, a regulated electric utility serving customers in Oklahoma and western Arkansas.

providers.name: Evergy
providers.description: Profile for Evergy in the API Evangelist network. Fortune F1000 (rank 539).

providers.name: Alliant Energy
providers.description: Fortune 1000 company Alliant Energy. Public API documentation has not yet been catalogued in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Duke Energy
providers.description: Duke Energy is one of the largest electric power holding companies in the United States, supplying electricity and natural gas to millions of customers across the Southeast and Midwest.

providers.name: Pinnacle West Capital
providers.description: Pinnacle West Capital is a holding company whose principal subsidiary is Arizona Public Service, the largest electricity utility in Arizona.

providers.name: Sempra
providers.description: Sempra is a North American energy infrastructure company with operations in Texas, California, Mexico, and emerging markets, serving utility customers and developing energy networks.
